rules.covers: Retention: personal data tables have a scheduled deletion task. Does not verify the 2-year period, and selects nothing until a table carries the retained tag.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Delete user's data everywhere when the account is deleted
No personal data kept longer than 2 years (the period itself)
Deciding which tables are retained and which records to delete or anonymise

assumptions: The 'retained' tag is the one the RET-002 template example uses. I did not invent a tag set.
Personal-data tables are those with user or customer identifiers or personal fields, judged from the schema files.
The retention scope applies to tables; no check reads a record's age.
confusions: The skill says a policy's rules must match catalogue names, but table.coverage_required's scope param 'tags' sits next to referenced_by in the template. I put it at the same level in params; it parsed, but I could not confirm from docs that a top-level tags param is a scope param for this check.
The parse output dropped the severity line when printing the normalized policy, though the file has it. Not clear whether that is a display issue or the parser ignored it.

Nothing in the catalogue covers a deletion cascade (data removed across all tables referencing a user). The closest is table.coverage_required, which only checks that some task deletes from a tagged table.
Retention age (2 years) is a runtime value; statement.param_bound bounds literal numbers only, so I found no check for it.

The skill's 'Never write a policy the workspace cannot support' guidance is clear for the tag case, but I had to decide whether to ship a policy that checks nothing today. I shipped it as advisory with a note in the reply.
wished_for: A check that verifies a delete function reaches every table with a reference to the deleted entity (a deletion-cascade check).
A check or param that reads a retention age from a timestamp field (e.g. created_at older than N days).
A recipe showing how to tag tables for a template's scope, and how the tag set is agreed with the team.
parse_errors_seen: RET-002.R1: tags "retained" is on no table on this branch, so it selects nothing. (warning, not an error)
why_confidence: The retention rule parses but checks nothing until a table is tagged, and it verifies only that a cleanup task exists, not the 2-year period. The erasure half has no matching check. I did not run policy evaluate, which the brief forbids.
